newsitem.title: AUSTRALIA: RTRS-Australian Broadcasting Corp Midday Update.
newsitem.headline: RTRS-Australian Broadcasting Corp Midday Update.

text.p: FOREIGN MINISTER, DOWNER TO VISIT EUROPE
Foreign Affairs Minister, Alexander Downer's, announced he will visit France, Germany and the United Kingdom from next week. It will be Mr Downer's first visit to Europe as Foreign Minister.
He will meet with leaders including French Prime Minister, Alain Juppe, German Foreign Minister, Klaus Kinkel and British Deputy Prime Minister, Michael Heseltine.
Mr Downer will also address the United Nations General Assembly in New York and continue to pursue Australia's case for a seat on the UN Security Council.
QLD POLICE MINISTER REJECTS GUN ARGUMENT
Queensland's Police Minister Russell Cooper has rejected a suggestion that the state will be the weak link in national gun laws.
The suggestion's come from the state convenor of the National Coalition for Gun Control, Helen Gadsten, who's concerned that people simply have to say they're collectors to get a licence.
But Mr Cooper says collectors will have to undergo stringent checks and must render their guns temporarily inoperable although he concedes this process can be reversed.
Around 6,000 workers in all sectors of the sugar industry are to strike for 24 hours on Thursday, saying the blame for any losses incurred during the strike will be with the Queensland government.
Queensland ACTU secretary, John Thompson, says the strike will protest against proposed changes to the Workers' Compensation Act.
Mr Thompson says he regrets the fact that the strike will cost canegrowers, but says it's the Government's fault because it hasn't given in to opposition to the proposals.
QLD GOVT MOVES TO GET LAND FOR PORT
The Queensland Government has moved to secure land for mining company Century Zinc's port facility which will service its proposed zinc mine in the far north west of the state.
The Government is to compulsorily acquire native title rights and interests on five lots at the Port of Karumba based on a request by Century Zinc for 40-year leases to be granted.
The Government advertised its intentions in the weekend press, saying Century Zinc has requested the leases be granted for the conduct of works.
Under Section 30 of the Acquisition of Land Act 1967, anyone wishing to become a native title party to the application must be a registered native title claimant before November 15 this year.
